bullets.title: Understanding Pregnancy and Antenatal Care
bullets.text: Pregnancy produces major physiological and emotional changes. Most are normal adaptations, but some findings indicate risk. Antenatal nursing care supports maternal wellbeing, monitors fetal growth, promotes healthy choices and identifies problems early.

bullets.title: Nursing Care During Labour and Birth
bullets.text: Labour is a dynamic process requiring ongoing assessment of the woman, fetus, contractions, pain, progress and emotional wellbeing. The nurse provides comfort, information, advocacy and timely escalation when labour deviates from the expected pattern.

bullets.title: Postnatal Recovery and Maternal Wellbeing
bullets.text: The postnatal period involves rapid physical and emotional adjustment. Nurses monitor recovery, support feeding, promote bonding and identify complications such as haemorrhage, infection, thromboembolism and mental-health concerns.

bullets.title: Essential Newborn Assessment and Care
bullets.text: The newborn must adapt rapidly to breathing, temperature control, feeding and circulation outside the uterus. Nurses support this transition, perform systematic assessment and teach families how to care safely for their baby.
